channel.title: Carat Capital — The Trade Paper of the Jewelry World
channel.description: Prices, intelligence and analysis from every desk of the stone trade: diamonds, gold and metals, gemstones, watches, auctions, retail and technology.

item.title: The Fed holds, three dissent, and gold slips to $4,029
item.description: Kevin Warsh's Fed kept rates at 3.50–3.75% in a 9–3 vote, with three presidents pushing for a hike. Gold eased from about $4,046 to near $4,029 as the guidance vanished.

item.title: Silver backs off $60 as the white metals cool
item.description: Silver traded near $57.90, off the $59 handle it wore on Monday; platinum slid to about $1,597 and palladium to roughly $1,248. The month's white-metal run paused into the Fed.

item.title: Tiffany and Bulgari carry LVMH as the group slips 3%
item.description: LVMH's Watches & Jewellery arm posted €5.23 billion in first-half sales, up 9% organically and 11% in the second quarter, while overall group revenue fell 3%. It was the group's best-performing division.

item.title: Boucheron hits a record as Kering's jewelry runs 14% ahead
item.description: Kering's jewelry houses lifted first-half revenue to €521 million, up 14% and 20% on a comparable basis, with operating income doubling to €32 million. Group revenue still fell 3% to €7.22 billion.

item.title: Petra's revenue caves as the small-stone squeeze bites
item.description: Fourth-quarter revenue fell to $38 million, down 44% from the prior quarter, as weak tender prices hit smaller goods. Net debt climbed to $322 million and Finsch entered a business-rescue process.

item.title: Gem Diamonds leans on the giants while the market stays soft
item.description: Where Petra caved, Gem Diamonds' Letšeng kept firing high — average prices rose about 17% to roughly $1,501 a carat, and a 191.82-carat white recovery led a run of exceptional stones that carried its numbers.

item.title: Rio's diamond unit fades to $118 million as Diavik winds down
item.description: First-half diamond sales fell 27% to $118 million and output dropped 51% to 1.1 million carats after Diavik's March closure. The unit swung to a $72 million EBITDA loss as Rio counts down its last diamond mine.

item.title: Who's still buying at $4,000 gold? India sends a mixed signal
item.description: The World Gold Council's July read on India shows record prices splitting the market — jewelry buyers trade down and lean on old-gold exchange while investment demand and imports stay firmer. The counter and the vault are diverging.

item.title: Gold idles at $4,046 as the Fed splits the room
item.description: Spot sits in a $4,021–$4,080 triangle on the eve of the July 29 decision. Futures price a 62% hold at 3.50–3.75% but a 38% hike, and 81% odds of a September move.

item.title: Silver eyes $60 as palladium jumps and platinum firms
item.description: While gold idles, the white metals move: palladium added 3.3% and platinum 1.7% on Monday to about $1,268 and $1,612, and silver near $58 keeps $60 in view — up more than 50% on the year.

item.title: Titan makes it three: revenue up 41% on India's gold counter
item.description: The Tanishq owner's June quarter grew 41 percent — a third straight quarter above 40 — with jewellery up 39, watches 23 and eyewear 23. Buyers rose in the early double digits; the average ticket rose far faster.

item.title: A watch retailer takes the tariffs to court
item.description: California's Collective Horology sued the US over the Section 301 duties that have made Swiss watches at least 12.5 percent dearer since April 2025, arguing Washington skipped the country-by-country analysis the law requires.

item.title: Three fancy-color diamonds go up with no reserve
item.description: Bonhams' 300-lot California sale on Tuesday sets modest estimates on serious color — a pink-purple oval, a deep pink and a heart-shaped blue, each topping near $35,000–$50,000 — and lets a 70-carat necklace sell with no floor at all.

item.title: Doha opens a diamond exchange, and eyes Dubai's lane
item.description: The Qatar Free Zones Authority launched the Qatar Diamond Exchange this week — a Kimberley-compliant hub at Ras Bufontas with sorting, vaulting and tenders under one roof, and the Gulf's newest bid to sit alongside Dubai.

item.title: The trade's price book bends to ruby
item.description: GemGuide pushed Mozambique ruby prices sharply higher and scrapped its ten-point scale for Burma stones, pricing only four grades — an admission that fine ruby is now too scarce to chart the usual way.

item.title: India's big August show fills up early
item.description: GJEPC's IIJS Premiere returns to Mumbai on August 6–10 with pre-registration past 25,000, landing just as June gems-and-jewellery exports jumped 26.5 percent — a confident sourcing season into an uncertain tariff year.

item.title: Israel's diamond chief resigns as exports hit a record low
item.description: Nissim Zuaretz stepped down after two years with first-half exports at $2.4 billion, the lowest on record and down from roughly $7 billion at the 2015 peak. Dubai, lab-grown and a new 10% US tariff were all named.

item.title: Not lab-grown, synthetic: CIBJO moves to redraw the label
item.description: The confederation expects to strike "laboratory-grown" and "laboratory-created" from its Blue Book at a September 4 congress and mandate "synthetic" instead, joining Russia, India, the African producers and the GIA in a coordinated tightening of language.

item.title: Thirty-pointers run while the one-carat stalls
item.description: The RapNet index for 0.30-carat diamonds rose 4.2% in June, up from 2.1% in May, and 0.50-carat goods added 1.3%, while the one-carat slipped 0.7%. The recovery is real, and it is happening at the bottom of the carat scale.

item.title: Gold coils under $4,100 into a three-headline Fed week
item.description: Spot holds the low $4,000s with support at $4,022 and $3,964 and resistance at $4,100, as the Federal Reserve decides July 28–29 alongside second-quarter GDP and core PCE. A hold at 3.50–3.75% is widely expected; the messaging is the trade.

item.title: China pulls in 173 tonnes of gold in a single June
item.description: China imported about 173 tonnes of gold in June, its strongest monthly inflow since March 2024, lifting the first half toward 820 tonnes. Softer prices reopened the counter in the East just as Western funds turned cautious.

item.title: Patek, Rolex and AP pull away on the resale board
item.description: Morgan Stanley's second-quarter read puts value retention at 15.4% above retail for Patek Philippe, 9.8% for Rolex and 3.0% for Audemars Piguet, while every other tracked brand sits below list, Cartier at −27.4% and Omega at −32.3%.

item.title: Seventy carats, no reserve, on the block at Bonhams
item.description: A 70-carat diamond necklace of pear, oval and marquise stones carries a top estimate near $50,000 and no reserve when Bonhams sells more than 300 California jewels on July 28, alongside pieces by Van Cleef & Arpels, Graff and Boucheron.

item.title: The GIA turns a light on fluorescence
item.description: From the fourth quarter the laboratory will add language to its reports separating fluorescence that changes a diamond's look from fluorescence that does not, addressing a stigma that has discounted a quarter to a third of all stones since the 1990s.

item.title: Up nine percent, and the average ticket did the lifting
item.description: US jewelry revenue rose 8.6% in the first half and 13% in June, but the average purchase price climbed about 19 to 20 percent. Fewer buyers, spending more: bracelets, pearls and higher-priced pieces carried the gain.

item.title: Chow Tai Fook up fifteen, and gold by the gram did it
item.description: Chow Tai Fook's quarterly retail sales rose 15.1%, with Hong Kong and Macau up 44.8% and weight-based gold jewelry up 64% there as softer gold revived demand. Luk Fook gained 32%, Chow Sang Sang 16%.

item.title: Silver up two percent, and the gold ratio tightens to 69
item.description: Silver added about 2% on Friday to roughly $58 while gold held near $4,061, compressing the gold-silver ratio to about 69.5 from 70.7 at midweek. Both metals mark time before the Fed's July 29 decision.

item.title: Antwerp runs short of goods, and the buyers turn to India
item.description: A summer shortage of polished goods in Antwerp is steering buyers toward India, where small-stone prices are recovering and the IIJS show opens August 6. A new 10% US duty hangs over the whole trade.

item.title: Diavik is closed, and Rio Tinto still pulled 33,000 carats from it
item.description: Rio Tinto recovered 33,000 carats from Diavik's remaining ore in the second quarter, months after the Canadian mine closed. Output fell 97% from a year earlier; the company will sell its final diamonds through year-end.

item.title: Anglo picks the Penny group for De Beers, and starts a year-end clock
item.description: Anglo American has named the Gareth Penny-led consortium its leading bidder for De Beers and expects to finalize the sale by the end of 2026, even as a two-year production pause looms at the Venetia mine.
